newsitem.title: UK: European aluminium physical premiums drop off.
newsitem.headline: European aluminium physical premiums drop off.

text.p: The summer doldrums have hit European physical markets with business in copper tailing off and aluminium premiums easing back, traders said on Friday.
"Premiums are coming lower as summer approaches. People who are sitting on metal need to get rid of it or end up carrying it all season," an aluminium physicals trader said.
Traders said availability of Russian A7E aluminium in Rotterdam was good. It was cited as trading this week at a premium of $39 and $40 to London Metal Exchange (LME) cash.

That was down sharply from the start of the month, when the same type of metal was reported to be trading at a $55 premium. Similarly, duty-paid Western aluminium was trading at $125, off $10 from levels quoted at the start of the month.

Three months prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were also off slightly from the beginning of June. Aluminium finished the midday kerb at $1,583, compared to around $1,600 at the start of the month.
The market was having difficulty hurdling stiff resistance at $1,600 and trading volumes on the LME were low, LME floor traders said.

Meanwhile in copper, European premiums have proved more stable this month, although physical business has stalled in Europe traders said. High cash prices, trading above $2,700 on Friday, were discouraging consumers from re-stocking, they said.
A fresh influx of what traders said was Chinese material into the market was another factor in the market.
"It's quiet, dull and dismal. Instead of stocking up, the Chinese are selling material back and taking profits because they don't want to buy at these levels," a trader said.
Grade A copper in Rotterdam was quoted at a premium of $15/$20 to LME cash, while metal in Italy was pegged at $20/$25. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
